title: Which part of the castle stops the attack?
instruction: For each attack, find the defence that stops it.
buckets: Second castle = a backup somewhere else

items.text: Attackers know about a bug in an old version of the browser and exploit it.
items.why: An update is a patch. It fixes a hole the attackers know about.

items.text: A torch app wants access to your contacts, location and microphone.
items.why: A torch only needs the light. Refuse the other permissions.

items.text: A website offers an “unlimited coins cheat” to download. Inside is a Trojan horse.
items.why: Install only from the official store. The guard doesn't let in strangers bearing gifts.

items.text: Ransomware encrypts all your photos and demands a ransom.
items.why: A copy in another place survives. You restore the photos and don't have to pay.

items.text: The system announces a security update
items.why: The update patches the hole before someone exploits it. Install it.

items.text: A horoscope quiz wants access to your text messages
items.why: The quiz doesn't need your messages. Don't allow the permission.

items.text: A friend sends a “new version of the game” to download outside the store
items.why: A fake file can come from a friend too. Download only from the official store.

items.text: Your phone falls into water and won't switch on
items.why: Only a backup that you keep somewhere other than your phone helps here.

debrief: Each defence stops a different attack. Updates patch the holes, permissions watch what an app may do, trusted sources keep fake programs out and a backup saves your data when everything else fails.
